reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight lies in treating peak age as a latent variable derived from noisy, incomplete longitudinal performance data. The framework combines a longitudinal model where performance y_ij is modeled as a noisy realization of a smooth trajectory f_i(t), plus a regression model for the latent peak age T*_i. This dual structure allows for principled handling of irregular sampling and measurement error. The use of an AFT model for T*_i enables incorporation of athlete-level covariates, such as training load or genetic markers, into the prediction of peak timing. The hierarchical Bayesian setup ensures that uncertainty in trajectory estimation is properly propagated to peak age inference and population-level effects. Simulation results confirm that this joint approach outperforms pseudo-peak methods in terms of reduced bias and accurate uncertainty quantification. The method's robustness under incomplete data makes it suitable for real-world applications like World Athletics rankings.
